headline: Approved updated Lyceum Committee bylaws unanimously and discussed spring 2026 "Celebration of Freedom" programming
summary: The committee reviewed and approved an updated draft of the Lyceum Committee bylaws with agreed-upon history language. Members also discussed plans for a spring 2026 "Celebration of Freedom" program with the high school, and noted a tentative November 14 AI event.
decisions: Approved the updated Lyceum Committee bylaws with agreed-upon history language, unanimously.

plain_text:
Page 1 of 2 
 
 
Gloucester Lyceum Committee      
Special Meeting 
Meeting Minutes 
Thursday, August 20, 2026 at 9 a.m.    
Zoom Only:    
As the recent amendments to the open meeting law allows, this Committee will continue to hold 
meetings remotely. Adequate alternative access to the meeting is provided through the zoom link 
below.                                                                    
https://us02web.zoom.us/j/86207455773 
Dial in at 646-931 3860 US 
 
 
Attendance: Julia Brotherton (Chair), Meredith Fine, Stephen Foley, Stan Franzeen, 
Martha Kurz, Steven Lewis, Douglas Richardson (signed off at 9:15), Leora Ulrich, 
William Waller, Ann Ziergiebel 
 
Not Present: Rebecca Aliberte 
 
 
1. Call to order  
 
2. Proposed Library Bylaws amendment: Lyceum Committee 
a. The Committee reviewed the updated draft of the Bylaws.  
b. Steven moved to accept the updated draft. Discussion ensued, and 
consensus was reached, on wording for the history of the Lyceum and 
the “legacy” aspect. Steven L moved to approve the bylaws with the 
agreed-upon history language. Martha seconded. The group thanked 
Meredith for her work. The motion passed unanimously.  
 
3. Spring 2026 Programming Discussion: “Celebration of Freedom”
Page 2 of 2 
 
a. Approaching high school for participation: We need to clarify details of 
the event (the format, the goal, the structure, who the audience is, etc.) 
before we can approach the high school.  
b. Annie proposed a topic of “What Does Freedom Look Like for You?”. 
This sentence would work well with the selection of Norman Rockwell 
paintings and could be in the center of the diagram. This would give the 
school a place to start.  
i. Meredith suggested that perhaps the Norman Rockwell Museum 
could offer some support. Meredith will reach out to them. 
c. Stephen F will draft a 30 to 50 word explanation of the theme to share 
with the school. We should include verbiage to ask the music teachers 
“what does freedom sound like?”. 
d. Tentative date for the event: Sometime in March.  
 
4. November AI event (AI Promise and Peril: A Conversation): Tentatively 
scheduled for November 14. 
 
5. Next Meeting: Thursday September 10, 2026 at 5:00 pm. 
 
6. 9:30 Adjourn. There being no further business the meeting was adjourned. 
 
Respectfully submitted, Tracy Bowen 
 
Motions Summary 
Steven L moved to approve the bylaws with the agreed-upon history language. 
Martha seconded and the motion passed unanimously 
 
Actions Summary 
Meredith suggested that perhaps the Norman Rockwell Museum could offer some 
support. Meredith will reach out to them. 
 
Stephen F will draft a 30 to 50 word explanation of the Celebration of Freedom 
theme to share with the school.
